items.title: Contains Duplicate aur Valid Anagram: ek hash map se dono
items.one_idea: Both Contains Duplicate and Valid Anagram are answered by remembering what you have already seen in a hash-based structure (a set of seen values, a count of each character), so no sorting or pair-checking is needed.
items.spoken_hook: Contains Duplicate problem, sorting के बिना एक loop में solve!
items.visual_idea: Row of six cells 4 7 1 9 7 3 with a pointer walking right and a seen box filling; at the second 7 the cell turns red; then count bars for listen and silent overlap, rat and car differ at t and c.
items.example: [4,7,1,9,7,3]: duplicate at step 5 with a set, 8 pair checks brute force; 10,000 numbers 49,995,000 pairs; listen/silent True, rat/car False.
items.check_question: Is [3,8,3] a duplicate? Are aab and abb anagrams? (yes, no)
facts_to_verify: Contains Duplicate hash table O(n) time/space, sorting O(n log n) (doocs 0217) - verified
Valid Anagram counting O(n) time, O(C) space, C=26 (doocs 0242) - verified
Counter is a dict subclass; hash lookup average O(1), worst O(n)

items.title: Recursion aur call stack: har call ka apna frame
items.one_idea: A recursive function calls itself on a smaller input until a base case returns; each active call keeps one frame on the call stack, so a missing base case or too much depth ends in a RecursionError (stack overflow).
items.spoken_hook: Recursive function चलाया, RecursionError आ गया!

hook_candidates.text: Recursive function चलाया, RecursionError आ गया!
Recursion में हर call का अपना stack frame बनता है।
Recursive function खुद को call करे, तो memory में क्या होता है?

items.hook_source: relatable_stake is the oldest of the last six (only d005); the error is the real one an engineer meets, with the standard term and no undefined word; d005 used the same wrong-way-first idea so this compares it on a concept day
items.hook_10s: Recursive function चलाया, RecursionError आ गया! Recursion यानी function खुद को छोटे input पर call करे। हर call stack पर अपना frame रखता है, और base case पर रुकता है। [frame 0: a stack of call boxes growing upward past a red limit line, label RecursionError]
items.visual_idea: A vertical call stack: fact(5) pushes frame boxes fact(5), fact(4) down to fact(0) one by one with n in each, then the returns pop from the top while the value 1, 1x1, 2, 6, 24, 120 builds up; second panel removes the base case and the stack keeps growing until it crosses a red limit line at depth 1000 and turns into RecursionError.
items.everyday_anchor: none: developer audience, no everyday analogies (owner 2026-10-26)
items.example: fact(5): 6 calls, max depth 6, returns 120; fact without base case: RecursionError 'maximum recursion depth exceeded' at depth 999 counted from the call; total(10000) recursive fails, loop gives 50005000. Run on CPython 3.12.3 (EXAMPLE limits are platform and version dependent).
items.check_question: What does f(n) = n * f(n-1) do with no base case? (RecursionError)
facts_to_verify: Each active call has one stack frame typically holding arguments, return address (if saved on the stack) and locals; push on call, pop on return; say 'typically', not 'always' (Wikipedia Call stack, researcher-verified)
Base case returns directly; recursive case breaks into smaller sub-problems; unbounded recursion typically exhausts stack space (Wikipedia Recursion, verified)
RecursionError is raised when the maximum recursion depth is exceeded (Python exceptions docs, verified)

Default limit 1000 is NOT in the sys docs; it is Py_DEFAULT_RECURSION_LIMIT 1000 in CPython 3.12 source (pycore_ceval.h). Say 'CPython's default' and say 'about 1000'; never 'the Python docs say 1000'
O(n) stack space for depth n has no fetched source: present it as 'n frames for depth n' shown by the run, not as a cited claim, unless the researcher finds a source

Run the code and show its real output: fact(5)=120 (6 calls with the n==0 base case; researcher counted 5 for a base case at n==1, so match the code shown on screen); no-base-case RecursionError 'maximum recursion depth exceeded' at depth about 999; total(10000) fails, loop gives 50005000; fact(5000) also fails
Optional: naive fib(5) 15 calls, fib(30) 2692537 calls (researcher-run, CPython 3.12.3); keep out unless the script needs a second example
